maya: FYI — seeing multiple customer reports of intermittent 504 / gateway timeouts for hosted inference endpoints since ~2026-03-16T22:04Z. Tickets: C-2412, C-2415. Example response snippet: `HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout` trace_id=tr_0a1b2c request_id=req_9f8e7d.
alan: :rotating_light: SRE dashboard shows memcache connection errors and a spike in backend latency to the KV layer at the same time window. conn_rejects + auth timeouts up ~14x.
jess: Pasted proxy log (excerpt):
```
2026-03-16T22:04:12Z proxy[req_id=req_9f8e7d] upstream_status=504 upstream_time=610ms backend=memcached-10.2.4.5:11211 err="handshake timeout"
2026-03-16T22:04:13Z runtime[trace=tr_0a1b2c] cache_fanout=64 backend_latency_ms=720 p95=6200
```
maya: Customer repro steps from C-2412: send 40 concurrent requests with ~8k-token prompts. When cache behaves badly, requests pile up and gateway returns 504s. P95 latency normally ~1.8s, now hitting 6-8s and lots of 502/504.
oscar: Working mitigation plan: temporarily increase cache RPC timeout, enable cache-bypass header flag for affected customers, and throttle prefetch fanout. Will push config change to hosted control plane.
alan: SRE findings: memcached node 10.2.4.5 shows repeated `auth-err: handshake timeout` and `connection reset` in system logs. Pool saturation observed on the proxy side (max open conns reached). Suspecting intermittent network flaps between edge and cache cluster. Opening network ticket.
jess: Root cause hypothesis: aggressive prefix prefetch in runtime fans out hundreds of key reads per request for large contexts. If memcached responds slowly, that multiplies into a thundering connection storm and pool exhaustion. Proposed short-term runtime changes: reduce `prefetch.max_fanout` to 8, add jitter to prefetch backoff, and circuit-breaker to fallback to cold-cache.
maya: Draft customer message prepared — apology + explanation + workaround (add `X-Redwood-Cache-Bypass: 1` to requests or set `cache_bypass=true` in SDK). Asking billing for temporary credits.
kevin: On billing — recommend auto-credit for impacted API calls that returned 5xx between 22:04Z and 22:40Z. Propose 10% credit for affected customers; needs approvals.
oscar: Deploying config patch now: `cache.timeout_ms=300`, `cache.prefetch.max_fanout=8`, `cache.fail_open=true` (temporary). Rolling to hosted region-a, region-b. ETA ~9m.
alan: Observability changes pushed: new dashboards for memcached auth_errors, conn_rejects, and prefetch fanout. Added alert on pool saturation > 80% for 2m. Also triggered failover of memcached pool to hot standby for cluster 10.2.x.
jess: Repro steps for devs to validate: run `./tools/load-test.sh --host https://api.redwood/v1 --concurrency 50 --requests 500 --prompt long_prompt.json` with `REDWOOD_CACHE_BYPASS=0` to simulate cache-on behavior. Example failing output: `504 gateway timeout (upstream_time=612ms)`. Attach logs and trace ids.
maya: Support actions: 1) apply workaround for affected tenants (enable cache-bypass), 2) notify customers with mitigations + credits note, 3) mark tickets P0 and attach tracer logs.
oscar: Network team ticket created: NET-8472 (possible route flap to memcached cluster).
alan: Follow-up items: confirm memcached auth handshake root cause (auth proxy or node restart bug), verify hot-standby health for 2h, and plan maintenance to rotate keys if needed.
kevin: Billing asked for list of affected accounts and exact time window. Maya to provide csv.
maya: I'll push the customer message now and update C-2412/C-2415. Monitoring looks like error-rate falling after config roll — will watch for 2 hours. Thanks all. :eyes: :pray:
